generation.raw_text: {"status":"answered","answer":"Mendel’s monohybrid experiment involved crossing two pea plants that differed in just one trait. For example, he crossed a pure-breeding yellow seed plant (YY) with a pure-breeding green seed plant (yy). In the first generation (F1), all the offspring had yellow seeds, indicating that yellow is the dominant trait. When these F1 plants were self-pollinated, the second generation (F2) showed a 3:1 ratio of yellow to green seeds. This experiment demonstrated the Law of Dominance, which states that in a pair of contrasting traits, one trait is dominant and appears in the F1 generation, while the other is recessive and reappears in the F2 generation.","selected_evidence_ids":["E2"],"citations":[{"evidence_id":"E2","pdf_page":191,"textbook_page":182}],"missing_information":[]}
